record.paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: For a connected unit-disk graph UDG(P) modeling a wireless ad hoc network on a planar point set P, reduce the total number of broadcast messages needed by a local distributed algorithm to compute a plane local spanner of UDG(P).

evidence.quote: Open Problem 22. Can one reduce the total number of messages in order to compute a plane local spanner of UDG(P)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P be a finite set of points in the plane. The unit-disk graph UDG(P) is the graph with vertex set P in which two points are adjacent if and only if their Euclidean distance is at most 1; assume UDG(P) is connected. A subgraph H of UDG(P) is called a plane spanner if H is planar (its straight-line embedding has no crossing edges) and there exists a constant t ≥ 1 such that for every pair u,v ∈ P, the length of a shortest path from u to v in H (sum of Euclidean edge lengths) is at most t times the length of a shortest path between u and v in UDG(P).

Consider the distributed model in which each node of UDG(P) is an autonomous processor that knows only its own coordinates and can communicate by local broadcast to all neighbors within unit distance. A distributed algorithm is called local if every node decides which of its incident edges belong to H using only information gathered from a constant-size neighborhood (e.g., its k-hop neighborhood for some constant k). The message complexity is the total number of broadcast messages exchanged during the execution of the algorithm.

Problem: Design a local distributed algorithm that, given a connected UDG(P) on n nodes, computes a plane spanner of UDG(P) using strictly fewer total broadcast messages than the previously known bound (e.g., better than the current best known O(n)-broadcast algorithms with their explicit constants), and determine the minimum achievable message complexity for this task.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work has continued to reduce the message complexity of distributed plane spanner construction in unit-disk graphs (e.g., algorithms achieving on the order of 5n broadcasts), and further improvements ("Improved Local Algorithms for Spanner Construction") have been published. However, no tight lower bound matches the upper bounds, and the question of the minimum message complexity for computing a plane local spanner of UDG(P) appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Improved Local Algorithms for Spanner Construction
status_evidence.snippet: Reducing the previous best known complexity of an algorithm to compute a planar spanner of a Unit Disk Graph to as few as 5n broadcasts.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work has reduced but not closed the message complexity bounds for distributed plane spanners of UDGs.

status_evidence.title: Local Construction of Planar Spanners in Unit Disk Graphs with Irregular Transmission Ranges
status_evidence.snippet: Local construction of planar spanners in unit disk graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Local distributed plane-spanner construction is an active area without a known optimal message complexity.

status_evidence.title: The Local Information Cost of Distributed Graph Spanners
status_evidence.snippet: Studies information-theoretic lower bounds for distributed spanner construction.
status_evidence.claim: Lower bounds for distributed spanner message complexity are still being investigated, suggesting the optimum is not yet known.
